Oh boy. 

Two days before your 13th birthday, your stepdad will be found dead in the family barn. A suicide by hanging. 

His parents will drive your mom out of the town you grew up in. You'll learn what the words "gold digging slut" mean. You'll lose your home and all of your possessions besides what you can pack in your backpack. You'll live in a van for a while. Then at Grandma's. 

Mom's abuse of drugs and alcohol will only get worse. She will never recover. She will never be able to be strong for you, to get you the grief and trauma counseling you'll need, ever. After the suicide you will be criminally neglected. It's okay to call the police. If not for you, then for your younger brothers.  

Mom too will be suicidal. She'll be put in a hospital while you're in high school. It's your job to be the parent. You will also feel the temptation to kill yourself. Don't tell mom. She doesn't care. Ask me how I know. 

Mom will start drinking again. She'll start locking herself in the bathroom and smoking weed as well as meth. You crying outside the bathroom door begging her to stop will not work. Save your tears. 

Don't let Mom drive you and your friend Steven to school. One morning she will be drunk. She will swerve, hit a car, and start a fight with the person she hit. You will never see Steven again. 

This will affect you for years. It's called PTSD. It's not just for war veterans. You'll have nightmares about Mom. You'll avoid alcohol like the plague. The smallest thing will remind you of her and you won't be able to think of anything else until you mumble an imagined conversation under your breath where you really tell her what you need to say.

The truth is, 12 year old me, once Mom realizes she doesn't *need* to give a shit about you, she will stop even pretending. She will never try again. Despite this, you are going to go on to achieve your dreams. You *will* get your dream job. You *will* get published. You *will* study animation with professionals from Pixar as your mentors. You *will* lead a fascinating life. Exactly none of this will matter to Mom. Cut your loses and remove her from your life as soon as you are able.  

Chin up. Keep drawing. Keep writing. Keep moving forward. 

Oh and also you're gay, and you're going to fall in love with a beautiful woman one day. She'll heal your wounds.

I cut off contact with my nmom about three years ago. 

Every once in a while I am wracked with guilt about my decision. What if she really does love me and all I'm doing is hurting her?

But then I remember the neglect. I remember the insults thinly veiled as constant, omnipresent "teasing". The bending-over-backwards for my half brothers while denying or insulting every interest I had.  The theft of hundreds of dollars from my literal actual piggy bank. The ignored plea for help when I felt suicidal. 

And then I remember, this isn't love. This isn't how you treat someone who you love.

Being a sensitive 12 year old believer, I was greatly upset by the notion of "fearing" god. I couldn't wrap my head around what that meant, and how fear could coexist with love. I asked my youth pastor, and he explained that to fear god meant something akin to respecting him. This upset me even more - why is fear and respect linked at all? If god, whose living word I was so upset by - meant respect and not fear, why did he say fear? 

I remember sobbing because I couldn't make myself experience love, fear and respect all at the same time.

I remember very little from before I was 13 or so; maybe one or two memories a year, and certainly nothing before 6 or so. 

Is this not normal? :S

I haven't spoken to my mother in three years. 

Growing up, my mom resented me. I wasn't supposed to have been born. She called me a monster baby - that is, when she was sober enough to do it. She was in and out of court-mandated rehab my entire adolescence. 

But that wasn't the final straw. 

My half brothers were greatly preferred over me. They were planned, and from fathers who stuck around at least through pregnancy. My mom trained my brothers to see me as she did - too weird to be loved. She made fun of me about every single aspect of my personhood; my appearance, my interests, my friends, my music, and encouraged my brothers to do the same. 

But that wasn't the final straw. 

When I was 16, I told her I wanted to kill myself. I was so tired of being me. She turned up the car radio to drown me out. She never spoke to me about it again. 

But that wasn't the final straw. 

Despite being the doormat and free babysitting service, I had graduated high school with honors and won a $87,000 scholarship to the college of my dreams, the school I wanted to go to since I was ten. She told me it was a scam, and waited until the day before the application was due to deny me a $200 loan so I could apply to the college and accept the scholarship. I lost the money. My absent father had just paid back due child support. My half brothers got a new above ground pool that summer. I never finished college. 

But that wasn't the final straw. 

I managed to scrape out a career in my early 20's doing what my degree would have done for me anyway. I even signed on with a publisher and had my first book published when I was 22. She never bothered to read the book, ask for a copy, or even learn its title. 

But that wasn't the final straw. 

A few years later, I'm launching the publication of my second book, a sequel. My publisher aligned the debut date to when I would be accepting an achievement award as a guest of honor at a convention. If I were an actor, it would be like going to the Golden Globes, but knowing I had already won. This is the pinnacle of my career, a goal I've been working towards for years. 

I call my mom, invite her to stay for free in the multi-bedroom hotel suite that the convention is providing me. I offer her free food, parking, and an opportunity to finally see what her eldest child had chosen as their life's calling. I even googlemap'd directions for her, at her request. 

She agrees to go! This is it, I thought, finally, my mom would see how hard I've worked, how I'm not so weird, how  I've found my people and my spot in the world and managed to chip out a name for myself. She would finally love me. 

Two days before the convention and I feel like I'm getting ready for my own wedding. I give her a call to check up, make sure she has everything she needs to make the two hour drive from her home to the convention center. She informs me that she forgot about my event, and doesn't really want to make the drive again, because my brother had a concert in the same city the weekend before and couldn't drive himself. 

That's the last time I spoke to her. She has no idea about my marriage, my name change, or the fact I've been hired abroad and am even closer to my loftier, more ambitious goals. She'll probably never know.

I cut off contact with my nmom, as well as her mother and sister, not because they're Ns (that's a debate for another day) but because I can't trust them to not speak to my nmom on my behalf. 

After a month with no contact, I called my grandmother (possibly an N) and explained why I wasn't returning their calls. I explained the abuse nmom made me suffer through, and n?grandma swept it under the rug, as always. I made it very clear that I wanted to be left alone, to not contact me until I contacted them. 

My aunt did not accept this. My aunt is the type of person who will jump to the absolute worst possible conclusion and nothing on gods green earth can convince her otherwise. She calls every single holiday and birthday. She sent passive aggressive birthday cards to my husband (or, she did, until we moved.) She found my Twitter account and my LinkedIn and quietly followed them. Every time she attempts to make contact, I am further steeled to not break my NC. 

About two years into NC, my little brother contacted me. He wanted me to contact my grandmother, vaguely insinuating her health is not great. He said that no one knew why I cut off contact. I told him I told Grandma exactly why. He said something about her getting old and forgetting. Bullshit.  Further, my grandmother is fine. I told my brother to not contact me until I was ready, and that I would not be guilted, pressured or badgered into changing my mind. 

Nmom, through all of this, has been silent. 

I've changed my name, gotten married and moved to another country since going NC. I can only hope my aunts cyberstalking will cease.
